description: AULA F75 Max host layer. The board's own firmware makes its F-row emit F13-F22, codes no physical keyboard produces. This file is the only place those codes get meaning. Space, CapsLock and every other key are left stock.

F13.note: Undo on tap, redo on hold. SolidWorks and Excel never adopted Ctrl+Shift+Z, so they get Ctrl+Y.

F14.note: Focus-or-launch the two most-switched-to non-CAD apps: Chrome 16.2 percent of focus events, Outlook 5.8 percent.

focusApp.note: Outlook classic. New Outlook (olk.exe) is also installed but unused.

F15.note: Tap flips to the previous window. Hold opens the switcher and keeps it open: each further press of the key advances one window, releasing commits.

F16.note: SolidWorks is 19.1 percent of all app switches, the single biggest target. Explorer on hold: activate an existing browser window, else open a new one.

focusApp.note: explorer.exe always runs as the shell, so the window class is what distinguishes a real file browser window from the desktop and taskbar.

F17.note: The Adobe pair: InDesign 12 percent of switches, Photoshop 5.5 percent. Both point at the Beta builds, which are the live installs on this machine.

focusApp.note: Photoshop Beta ships the same exe name as the shipping builds; the Beta is the only live install here and owns the App Paths default.

F18.note: Media keys sit on F18/F21 because the telemetry cannot see them: they never reach an app, so there is no evidence they earn a better key.

F19.note: Sticky num layer toggle. Tap-only, so it fires on key-down with zero delay.

F20.note: Paste 778 times and copy 443 times in 13 days, the two highest-count chords measured. Tap gets the more frequent one.

F21.note: See F18 on why media landed here.

F22.note: Save on tap, Save As on hold.

num.note: Right-hand numeric pad. Toggled by F19, stays on until toggled off. Space is deliberately absent: it stays a plain Space.
